origins.base layer: Essential packages of the pinned Debian trixie-slim base (glibc, util-linux, ncurses, acl, zlib, perl-base), identical to the agent image's base-layer group in scan/baseline/timelike-agent.json, whose reasoning applies. Debian publishes no fixed package in trixie or trixie-security (Grype: wont-fix or not-fixed), so no fix is available. Unlike the agent image, the vanilla image keeps Debian's 11 setuid/setgid binaries (mount, umount, su, passwd, chfn, chsh, gpasswd, newgrp, chage, expiry, unix_chkpwd), deliberately: it is the unmodified baseline timelike is compared against. The local privilege-escalation findings therefore rely on no-new-privileges, not on the binaries' absence: In the bench, every task container runs as uid 1000 with --network none, --cap-drop ALL and no-new-privileges (bench/benchlib/docker.py), and bench/run.sh refuses a run with any key-shaped variable in the driver, either image's ENV or a task container. The rest are memory or resource bugs in library calls the bench's tasks do not reach with hostile input.
origins.files under /opt/agent: The agent runtimes, built by the same runtimes stage as the agent image (feature 007 slice 1), with their stock behaviour. The agent image's 'files under /opt/agent' group and its entries' reasons apply; in the bench, task containers have no network, so npm's registry cache is not reached at all there.
origins.git: Pulled in by git (libcurl3t64-gnutls, libexpat1, perl, libperl5.40, perl-modules-5.40; libsasl2-2 and libsasl2-modules-db through libcurl3t64-gnutls and libldap2), identical to the agent image's git group, whose reasoning applies. The vanilla image's purpose is 'Debian + git'. No fixed package in trixie or trixie-security. In the bench, task containers have no network at all (--network none), so no libcurl transfer happens, and they hold no credentials. In the bench, every task container runs as uid 1000 with --network none, --cap-drop ALL and no-new-privileges (bench/benchlib/docker.py), and bench/run.sh refuses a run with any key-shaped variable in the driver, either image's ENV or a task container.

findings.reason: Use-after-free that needs CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS followed by curl_easy_reset. git's http transport never sets HTTP/2 stream dependencies. Bench context: vanilla task containers run with --network none and hold no credentials, so no transfer occurs. Re-review if a bench task container is ever given a network or credentials (for example live runs), and at feature 12.

Digest Authorization header carried to a second origin on a reused handle. The agent holds no credentials in slice 0 (P4): no credential helper, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, empty askpass, so no Authorization header exists to leak. Re-review when Adele (feature 12) brokers credentials. Bench context: vanilla task containers run with --network none and hold no credentials, so no transfer occurs. Re-review if a bench task container is ever given a network or credentials (for example live runs), and at feature 12.

Use-after-free in HTTP/2 server push with shared connections. Server push needs a push callback (CURLMOPT_PUSHFUNCTION), which git's http transport does not set. Bench context: vanilla task containers run with --network none and hold no credentials, so no transfer occurs. Re-review if a bench task container is ever given a network or credentials (for example live runs), and at feature 12.

Negotiate (SPNEGO) connection reuse after an empty-credential request. The image has no Kerberos credentials and sets no http.emptyAuth, and the agent holds no credentials at all (P4), so there is no authenticated connection for another request to ride on. Re-review when Adele (feature 12) brokers credentials. Bench context: vanilla task containers run with --network none and hold no credentials, so no transfer occurs. Re-review if a bench task container is ever given a network or credentials (for example live runs), and at feature 12.

Pulled in by git, which uses expat only for http-push over WebDAV, which timelike does not use. Not caused by 007 slice 1: it is in the base layer's git and would block master too. libsasl2-2 and libsasl2-modules-db 2.1.28+dfsg1-9 (CVE-2026-107161): heap overflow in the DIGEST-MD5 client plugin when a server's challenge needs quoting. No Debian fix (Grype: not-fixed). Not in the base layer: the pinned trixie-slim base installs neither (its dpkg status, read 2026-10-09); git brings them in through libcurl3t64-gnutls -> libldap2 -> libsasl2-2 -> libsasl2-modules-db (Debian trixie's Depends). Not caused by 008 slice 1: it would block master too. Revisit when Debian ships a fix.

npm's bundled http-cache-semantics 4.2.0 (GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp, alias CVE-2026-93748): max-stale handling can serve a cached response across users. No fixed release exists. In npm it decides freshness for npm's own registry cache, which here is per user (~/.npm of the one agent user) and holds public package metadata: there is no second user whose responses could be disclosed. GnuTLS 3.8.9 (Debian 3.8.9-3+deb13u4), the TLS library of git's https transport (libcurl3t64-gnutls). CVE-2026-67693: an end-entity certificate with a contradictory Key Usage and Extended Key Usage is not rejected. As the advisory describes it (Grype's text, read 2026-10-10), the flaw is in the usage checks, not in chain or host-name verification, so a peer still needs a certificate for the host from a CA in the image's trust store (ca-certificates). The agent holds no credentials in its fetches here (P4), which bounds what an accepted peer could obtain. No Debian fix (Grype: not-fixed). Not in the base layer: the pinned trixie-slim base installs none of the Kerberos or GnuTLS libraries (its dpkg status, 78 packages, read 2026-10-10); git brings them in through libcurl3t64-gnutls (Debian trixie's Depends: libcurl3t64-gnutls -> libgnutls30t64 and libgssapi-krb5-2; librtmp1 and libngtcp2-crypto-gnutls8 -> libgnutls30t64; libgssapi-krb5-2 -> libkrb5-3, libk5crypto3, libkrb5support0). Checked from the base layer and the package index, not by dpkg in a built image (no Docker on the code host). Not caused by 005 slice 1: it would block master too. Revisit when Debian ships a fix.

GnuTLS 3.8.9 (Debian 3.8.9-3+deb13u4), the TLS library of git's https transport (libcurl3t64-gnutls). CVE-2026-88647 (Critical, its own reason): it BYPASSES HOST-NAME VERIFICATION on the Common Name path. As the advisory describes it (Grype's text, read 2026-10-12), a crafted certificate gets past the check that falls back to the certificate's Common Name, so a certificate issued for one host can be accepted for another. Unlike CVE-2026-95210, this is a host-name verification bypass, and the operator accepted it as such, on its own (2026-10-12T16:44:10Z, bridge/feedback/15-20261012-034908-lane-013s1-a2-target-cells-and-a-gnutls-critical.md, item 2). The bounds: the agent holds no credentials in its fetches (P4), so no credential can be read off a fetch; what a forged peer on the network path still can do is serve forged content to a git fetch over https, or read what the agent fetches. That is accepted as a bounded risk until Debian ships a fix, not as no risk. No Debian fix (Grype: not-fixed). Not in the base layer: the pinned trixie-slim base installs none of the GnuTLS libraries (its dpkg status, 78 packages, read 2026-10-10); git brings libgnutls30t64 in through libcurl3t64-gnutls, as for the four entries above. Not caused by 013 slice 1: it would block master too. Revisit when Debian ships a fix.
